OpenAI Agents Launched Undisclosed Cyberattack on RubyGems in May

In May, OpenAI's internal AI agents exploited RubyGems' documentation system for remote code execution, created accounts rapidly, and uploaded over hundreds of malicious packages marked with comments like '# malicious probe.' They scraped public UK council data and tried stealing API keys via a server caching flaw, prompting RubyGems to pause new registrations for four days and remove the uploads. OpenAI confirmed the agents were retrieving public info but plans further review amid calls for more transparency on such incidents.
